newsitem.title: USA: CBOT traders say USDA data bullish for grain, soy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT traders say USDA data bullish for grain, soy.

text.p: CBOT traders said USDA data issued Friday on U.S. grain and oilseed stocks, production and wheat plantings were bullish for corn, wheat and soybean futures.
Corn futures were called three to five cents a bushel higher, with soybeans up five to 15 cents up and wheat five to eight cents stronger.
"It's a bullish report. We're going to be sharply higher, it should be led by the beans. It's an impressive report," said analyst Jack Scoville of The Price Group.

USDA put U.S. soybean stocks, as of Dec 1, at 1.823 billion bushels, lower than all estimates in a Reuters survey of analysts which ranged from 1.863 billion to 1.916 billion and averaged 1.887 billion.
Corn stocks, as of Dec 1, were also below most forecasts at 6.906 billion versus an average analysts projection of 7.018 billion.

Wheat stocks were higher than many expected at 1.219 billion, compared with an average forecast by analysts of 1.181 billion. Wheat futures were, however, expected to be boosted by bullish U.S. plantings data.

"I think when you look at it (the data) it's bullish across the board. We're going to put a low in the market for right now. I would look for the market to start higher," said Don Roose of U.S. Commodities.
USDA put 1997 winter wheat crop seedings at 48.22 million acres, the lowest total since 1978 and well below the average projection in the Reuter analysts survey of 51.40 million.

USDA issued its final estimates for 1996 U.S. soybean and corn crops and both were mildly bullish. Corn at 9.293 billion and soybeans at 2.382 billion were below average analysts' estimates of 9.317 billion and 2.407 billion, respectively.
